mainTopic: Partial הגרמה and holes in the windpipe during שחיטה; where on the neck שחיטה and מליקה are done
overview: The amud opens in the middle of an argument. It explains why 'proper cut, הגרמה, proper cut' would be פסולה: the animal's life leaves during the bad middle third. The people of סורא ask רב נחמן about this case. He answers from רבי אלעזר בר מניומי's rule that a comb-shaped שחיטה is כשרה, but the גמרא pushes that proof off. רב כהנא then asks רב יהודה four questions. 'Proper, הגרמה, proper' is כשרה, and 'הגרמה, proper, הגרמה' is פסולה. Cutting right at a hole in the windpipe is כשרה, and running into a hole partway through is פסולה. רבי אלעזר compares the hole cases to a שחיטה shared by a גוי and a Jew, but רבי יוחנן dismisses this, and רבא explains why. A new משנה teaches that שחיטה is done from the front and sides of the neck while מליקה is done from the עורף, and the גמרא defines עורף from פסוקים. Finally, the sons of רבי חייא describe how מליקה is done, and the גמרא begins a proof about this that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the middle-הגרמה case is invalid: life leaves during the bad cut
steps.stepSummary: The speaker is told not to back down from ruling 'proper, הגרמה, proper' פסולה. Backing down would undo his earlier ruling, which was built on the same logic: what counts is which kind of cut was happening when the animal's life left.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you back down, you ruin your first ruling. There, why did you say it is valid? Because when the life went out, it went out during the valid cutting. Here too, when the life goes out, it goes out during the הגרמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is arguing that the ruling of פסול in the 'proper, הגרמה, proper' case must stand. It uses the same reasoning that made the opposite case כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of 'הגרמה, proper, הגרמה', the animal's life left during the middle third, which was a proper cut, so it is כשרה. By the same test, in 'proper, הגרמה, proper', the life leaves during the middle third, which is a הגרמה, so it is פסולה. Backing down on one ruling would break the logic of the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting above the proper area of the neck (toward the head), which makes a שחיטה invalid
The life (of the animal)
Goes out, leaves
You declare it valid (כשר)
The first one, here meaning the first ruling

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a sentence. 'If so' means 'if you back down from saying the middle-הגרמה case is פסולה'. It is not a brand-new idea.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a clear test: the status of a שחיטה depends on what kind of cut was being made at the moment the animal's life left.

phrases.english: For if so, you ruin the first one.
phrases.notes: 'If so' means if you back down. 'The first one' is your earlier ruling: הגרמה, then a proper cut, then הגרמה is valid.

phrases.english: There, what is the reason you declare it valid?
Because when the life goes out,
it goes out during its valid cutting.
Here too, when the life goes out,
it goes out during the הגרמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a discussion that began before this section, defending the ruling that 'proper, הגרמה, proper' is פסולה.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that 'proper, הגרמה, proper' is פסולה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reasoning behind the earlier ruling that 'הגרמה, proper, הגרמה' is כשרה: what matters is which cut was happening when the life left.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שחיטה follows the kind of cut that was happening when the animal's life left.

steps.title: The people of סורא ask רב נחמן about proper, הגרמה, proper
steps.stepSummary: When רב נחמן visits סורא, he is asked about a cut made of a proper third, then a third of הגרמה, then a proper third.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן happened to come to סורא. They asked him: if someone cut a third properly, did הגרמה on a third, and cut a third properly, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new conversation begins. The people of סורא ask רב נחמן a direct question about the same three-stage case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the exact one just discussed: the middle third is the הגרמה. Now the question goes to רב נחמן, who may see it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come, visited
They asked him
A third (of the windpipe)
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Nachman happened to come to Sura,
they asked him:
If one cut a third properly and did הגרמה on a third
and cut a third properly, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיקְּלַע רַב נַחְמָן לְסוּרָא, בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the same case as step 1 with a different sage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a שחיטה of 'proper third, הגרמה third, proper third' כשרה or פסולה?

steps.title: רב נחמן answers from the comb-shaped שחיטה rule
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says this is already covered by רבי אלעזר בר מניומי: a שחיטה shaped like a comb, going up and down, is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: isn't this the rule of רבי אלעזר בר מניומי? For רבי אלעזר בר מניומי said: a שחיטה made like a comb is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers that the case is כשרה. He points to an earlier rule that a zigzag cut, shaped like a comb, is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads 'like a comb' as a cut that goes up and down, partly in the proper area and partly in the הגרמה area. If so, a middle third of הגרמה would not make the שחיטה פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same as...?
Like a comb, meaning a jagged up-and-down cut
Valid
That is made (in a certain shape)

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן's answer seems to clash with step 1, where this same case was called פסולה. That is fine: these are two separate discussions. Also, the very next step questions his proof.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי,
phrases.english: He said to them: isn't this the rule of Rabbi Elazar bar Minyumi?
For Rabbi Elazar bar Minyumi said:
A שחיטה made like a comb is valid.
phrases.notes: Picture the teeth of a comb: the cut goes up and down instead of straight across.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is כשרה, based on רבי אלעזר בר מניומי's rule that a comb-shaped שחיטה is valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שחיטה shaped like a comb is כשרה.

steps.title: Maybe the comb case stays inside the proper area
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe רבי אלעזר בר מניומי meant a zigzag that never leaves the proper area for שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is within the place of שחיטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's proof. Maybe the comb case has no הגרמה in it at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the up-and-down cut stays inside the proper area, it tells us nothing about a cut that goes up into the הגרמה area. Then רבי אלעזר בר מניומי's rule does not answer the question the people of סורא asked. רב יהודה rules on this same case in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Within the proper area of the neck for שחיטה

phrases.english: But perhaps it is within the place of שחיטה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי אלעזר בר מניומי. It does not rule on the case itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source may describe a different case: a zigzag that stays inside the proper area.

steps.title: Why would that even need saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the whole cut is in the proper area, it is obviously valid. Why would רבי אלעזר בר מניומי need to teach that?
steps.simpleTranslation: Within the place of שחיטה, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the pushback from step 4. A rule that only says 'a cut in the right place is valid' seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sage's statement should teach something new. If the comb case is fully inside the proper area, the rule looks too obvious to need saying.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (It is obvious)

phrases.english: Within the place of שחיטה, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the comb case stays inside the proper area
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On that reading the rule is obvious, so there would be no reason to state it.

steps.title: It teaches that a cut need not be straight
steps.stepSummary: The rule is still needed: we might have thought a שחיטה must be a straight, clean cut. רבי אלעזר בר מניומי teaches that a jagged cut inside the proper area is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we need a clean, straight שחיטה, and this is not one. So it teaches us that it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 5. The comb rule does teach something new even if the cut stays inside the proper area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that a שחיטה does not have to be straight. So the reading from step 4 holds up, and רב נחמן's proof is no longer forced.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken first thought)
We require
Clear, open, straight across
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר בר מניומי's comb rule may only mean that a jagged cut inside the proper area is כשרה. So it does not prove that a third of הגרמה in the middle is acceptable, and רב נחמן's proof is pushed off.

phrases.english: You might have said: we require a clear, straight שחיטה
and that is not here, so it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: 'It teaches us' means רבי אלעזר בר מניומי is telling us the jagged cut is still כשרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and backs up the pushback of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement teaches something new (a 'מהו דתימא' answer)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שחיטה must be a clean, straight cut, so a jagged one would be פסולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A jagged שחיטה inside the proper area is כשרה. That is what the comb rule teaches.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן's proof from the comb rule is rejected. The case of 'proper, הגרמה, proper' is not settled by it.

steps.title: A memory-aid for the next discussion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, the letters בכ״ד, to help remember the order of the sages in the coming discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory-aid: בכ״ד.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a short memory-aid before starting the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for a sage who will speak next: ב for רבי אבא, כ for רב כהנא, and ד for רב יהודה. It is not a ruling, just a tool for remembering the order.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory-aid

phrases.english: (Memory-aid: בכ״ד.)
phrases.notes: These letters stand for the sages coming up next: רבי אבא, רב כהנא and רב יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the finished discussion to set up the next one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is only a memory-aid for the order of the coming sages.

steps.title: Cut a third, divert a third, then cut a third
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks about a cut that starts properly, wanders out of the proper area in the middle third, and finishes properly. רב יהודה says it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא sat behind רב כהנא, and רב כהנא sat in front of רב יהודה and asked: If someone cut one third properly, then let the knife slip out of the proper area for the next third, and then cut the last third properly, what is the law? רב יהודה answered: the שחיטה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene with the three sages from the סימן. Then it brings the first question and answer: proper, diverted, proper. Answer: כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the three thirds were cut in the proper place, so most of the windpipe was cut correctly. The diverted part in the middle does not ruin the שחיטה. The גמרא gives no reason, but the next question shows that the order and amount of proper cutting matter.

keyTerms.meaning: He diverted the knife: he cut outside the proper area of the neck (above the proper place on the windpipe).
One third of the windpipe.
What is the law? A standard way of asking a question.
His שחיטה is valid.
In front of him (as a student before his teacher).

steps.confusionAlert: הגרמה does not mean the cut was bad in its manner. It means the cut was in the wrong place, outside the area where שחיטה works.

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵיב רַבִּי אַבָּא אֲחוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba sat behind Rav Kahana,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַב כָּהֲנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: and Rav Kahana sat before Rav Yehuda,
and he sat and said:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב כהנא, asking his teacher רב יהודה.

phrases.english: If one cut a third properly and diverted the knife for a third
and then cut the last third properly, what is the law?
He said to him: His slaughter is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְתֵיב רַבִּי אַבָּא אֲחוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the names hinted at by the סימן בכ״ד. רב כהנא asks the same 'proper, הגרמה, proper' case raised in steps 1 and 2, and רב יהודה rules it כשרה. That is the opposite of the reasoning in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a שחיטה valid if only the middle third was diverted out of the proper area?

steps.title: Divert a third, cut a third, then divert a third
steps.stepSummary: Now the order is flipped: only the middle third is cut properly. רב יהודה says it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone diverted the knife for one third, cut the next third properly, and diverted again for the last third, what is the law? רב יהודה answered: the שחיטה is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא asks the mirror image of the first case. This time רב יהודה answers that the שחיטה is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case two thirds were cut properly. Here only one third was, which is less than most of the windpipe. Putting the two answers side by side shows the outcome depends on how much was cut in the right place, not just on whether some diverting happened.

keyTerms.meaning: His שחיטה is invalid. The animal is not permitted by this שחיטה.
And he cut properly, in the correct area.

phrases.english: If one diverted for a third and cut a third properly
and then diverted for the last third, what is the law?
He said to him: His slaughter is not valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ וְשָׁחַט שְׁלִישׁ וְהִגְרִים שְׁלִישׁ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of step 8, with the opposite ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a שחיטה valid if only the middle third was cut in the proper area?

steps.title: Cutting right where there is a hole
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks about cutting at the exact spot of a hole in the windpipe. רב יהודה says it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone made the cut right at the place where the windpipe had a hole, what is the law? רב יהודה answered: the שחיטה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The questions move to a new topic: a hole (נקב) in the windpipe. If the cut goes right through the spot of the hole, the שחיטה is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole in the windpipe could make the animal a טרפה. But when the knife cuts right where the hole is, the hole simply becomes part of the cut. So it does not ruin the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A hole or perforation (here, in the windpipe).
In the place of; at the exact spot of.

phrases.english: If one cut at the place of a hole, what is the law?
He said to him: His slaughter is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pair of sages, new kind of problem: a hole instead of a diverted cut.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does cutting at the spot of a hole in the windpipe ruin the שחיטה?

steps.title: The knife runs into a hole partway through
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks about a cut that reaches a hole in the middle of the שחיטה. רב יהודה says it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone was cutting and the knife reached a hole in the windpipe partway through, what is the law? רב יהודה answered: the שחיטה is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last of the four questions. Here the hole is met in the middle of cutting, and the שחיטה is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference from step 10 is timing. In the case explained here, the knife had cut half the windpipe when it reached the hole. Counting the hole, most of the windpipe was now open, but not most of it through proper cutting. So the hole, not the שחיטה, finished the job, and the שחיטה is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Met or ran into (the knife reached the hole).
An animal with a fatal defect, which שחיטה cannot make permitted.

steps.whatToRemember: Four quick rulings: (1) proper-diverted-proper = כשרה; (2) diverted-proper-diverted = פסולה; (3) cutting right at a hole = כשרה; (4) running into a hole partway through = פסולה. In the first pair, the apparent difference is how much was cut in the right place. For the hole pair, רבי אלעזר will explain the difference by order (like a גוי starting and a Jew finishing, or the reverse), but רבי יוחנן and רבא reject that distinction.

phrases.english: If one cut and encountered a hole, what is the law?
He said to him: His slaughter is not valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting case to step 10, with the opposite ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a שחיטה valid if the knife runs into a hole partway through?

steps.title: The rulings reach רבי יוחנן, who asks what the difference is
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's two rulings about the hole are passed along until they reach רבי יוחנן, who asks why the two cases should differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא went and told it to רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר went and told it to רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן said to him: What is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The rulings from steps 10 and 11 are carried from teacher to teacher until they reach רבי יוחנן. He asks why cutting right at the hole should be כשרה while running into the hole in the middle should be פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the knife meets the same hole in the windpipe. The only difference is timing: whether the hole is there at the start or is reached partway through. רבי יוחנן wants to know why timing should change the result.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? A request for the reason behind two different rulings
In front of him, in his presence

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba went,
and said it before Rabbi Elazar;
Rabbi Elazar went,
and said it before Rabbi Yochanan.
He said to him: What is the difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the difference between the rulings in steps 10 and 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a cut made at a hole is כשרה while a cut that runs into a hole midway is פסולה

steps.title: רבי אלעזר compares the cases to a שחיטה done partly by a גוי
steps.stepSummary: Cutting at the hole is like a גוי starting and a Jew finishing. Running into the hole is like a Jew starting and a גוי finishing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If he cut at the place of the hole, it is like a case where a גוי began the שחיטה and a Jew finished it. If he cut and then hit the hole, it is like a case where a Jew began and a גוי finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers רבי יוחנן's question with a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hole is treated like the part of the cut that 'doesn't count.' If the part that doesn't count comes first and a proper cut finishes the job, it is כשרה, like a Jew finishing after a גוי. If a proper cut comes first and the part that doesn't count finishes it, it is פסולה, like a גוי finishing after a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: A hole or perforation, here in the windpipe
Ran into, came upon
Finished, completed the cut

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר is now answering רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: If he cut at the place of a hole,

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁשָּׁחַט גּוֹי וְגָמַר יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: it becomes like one where a gentile cut and a Jew finished.
If he cut and came upon a hole,

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁשָּׁחַט יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגָמַר גּוֹי.
phrases.english: it becomes like one where a Jew cut and a gentile finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט בִּמְקוֹם נֶקֶב, נַעֲשָׂה כְּמִי שֶׁשָּׁחַט גּוֹי וְגָמַר יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The order matters: a bad part followed by a good finish is like גוי then ישראל (כשר); a good start followed by a bad finish is like ישראל then גוי (פסול).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן dismisses the comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן mockingly calls out 'גוי, גוי', rejecting רבי אלעזר's comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן called out about him: 'גוי, גוי!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the answer with a short, dismissive remark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not accept that a hole in the windpipe can be compared to a גוי doing part of the שחיטה. He gives no reason here. רבא supplies the reason in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He called out about him, said mockingly

steps.confusionAlert: 'גוי גוי' is not a new ruling about non-Jews. It is a dismissive way of saying 'you keep repeating the word גוי, but it doesn't fit here.'

phrases.english: He called out about him: "Gentile, gentile."
phrases.notes: He means: you keep saying 'גוי,' but that comparison doesn't belong here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison to a שחיטה done partly by a גוי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated here; רבא explains it in the next step.

steps.title: רבא explains why the גוי comparison fails
steps.stepSummary: With a גוי, the Jew never cut the majority, so the animal's life left through the גוי. With a hole, the same Jew does the whole cut, so the hole's position should not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יוחנן was right to call out 'גוי, גוי.' It makes sense there: the Jew was supposed to cut the majority and did not. So when the life left the animal, it left through the hand of the גוי. But here, after all, he is the one doing the whole שחיטה. What difference does it make to me whether he cut at the hole or ran into the hole?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up רבי יוחנן's dismissal and spells out exactly why the comparison breaks down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גוי case, a different, invalid person finishes the cut, so the death comes from him. In the hole case, one valid Jew does the entire cut, and the hole is just part of the windpipe. So the order of hole and cut gives no real reason to treat the two cases differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Well, correctly
It makes sense / granted (in one case, but not the other)
The majority, here the majority of the windpipe or food pipe
The animal's life
After all, since

steps.whatToRemember: רבא sides with רבי יוחנן. The גוי comparison fails because there one person never cut the majority, while with a hole the same Jew does the whole שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
He rightly called out about him "Gentile, gentile."
It makes sense there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the case where a Jew starts and a גוי finishes.

phrases.english: since the Jew should have cut the majority
and he did not cut it,
when the life went out,
it went out by the hand of the gentile.
But here, after all, he is the one slaughtering;
what difference is it to me if it was at the place of a hole,
or if he came upon a hole?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שַׁפִּיר קָרֵי עֲלֵיהּ גּוֹי גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's rejection
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אלעזר's comparison of the hole cases to a שחיטה shared by a ישראל and a גוי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With a גוי, the life leaves through an invalid person's hands; with a hole, one valid Jew does the entire שחיטה, so the hole's position makes no difference.

steps.title: משנה: the sides, nape, and throat for שחיטה and מליקה
steps.stepSummary: Cutting from the sides or the throat is valid for שחיטה but not for מליקה. From the nape it is the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who slaughters from the sides: his שחיטה is valid. One who does מליקה from the sides: his מליקה is invalid. One who slaughters from the back of the neck: his שחיטה is invalid. One who does מליקה from the back of the neck: his מליקה is valid. One who slaughters from the throat: his שחיטה is valid. One who does מליקה from the throat: his מליקה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares where on the neck you may do שחיטה (cutting with a knife) and where you may do מליקה (the כהן pinching a bird offering's neck with his fingernail).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the neck gets a pair of rulings. שחיטה works from the front (the throat) and from the sides. מליקה works only from the back (the nape). The two acts are opposites in where they must be done.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching: the כהן cuts a bird offering's neck from the back with his fingernail
The sides of the neck
The nape, the back of the neck
The throat, the front of the neck
Short for מתניתין, our משנה

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who slaughters from the sides: his slaughter is valid.
One who pinches from the sides: his pinching is invalid.
One who slaughters from the nape: his slaughter is invalid.
One who pinches from the nape: his pinching is valid.
One who slaughters from the throat: his slaughter is valid.
One who pinches from the throat: his pinching is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה is valid from the sides and throat and invalid from the nape; מליקה is valid from the nape and invalid from the sides and throat.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: what works for one fails for the other
steps.stepSummary: The whole nape is valid for מליקה and the whole throat is valid for שחיטה, so what is valid for one is invalid for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the whole back of the neck is valid for מליקה, and the whole throat is valid for שחיטה. It comes out that what is valid for שחיטה is invalid for מליקה, and what is valid for מליקה is invalid for שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason behind its list of cases and sums it up in one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every place on the nape works for מליקה, and every place on the throat works for שחיטה. Because they are opposite zones, a place that works for one act never works for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out, the result is
Valid / invalid

steps.whatToRemember: Front of the neck is for שחיטה; back of the neck is for מליקה. Each place that is valid for one is invalid for the other.

phrases.english: for the entire nape is valid for pinching,
and the entire throat is valid for slaughter.
It comes out: what is valid for slaughter is invalid for pinching,
and what is valid for pinching is invalid for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for and summary of the cases in step 16
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שחיטה and מליקה use opposite parts of the neck, so what is valid for one is invalid for the other.

steps.title: What does 'עורף' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה means by the word עורף.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'עורף'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking what the word עורף means. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that שחיטה from the עורף is invalid and מליקה from the עורף is valid. Before going further, the גמרא needs to know exactly which part of the neck is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The back of the neck or head

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is 'oref'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's rule to defining a key word in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the neck the word עורף refers to.

steps.title: It cannot mean the bone itself
steps.stepSummary: If עורף meant the actual bone, מליקה there would also be invalid, so the משנה would not single out שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the actual עורף, why mention only one who slaughters? Even one who pinches there would be invalid! The תורה said 'ממול ערפו', next to its עורף, and not the עורף itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simplest meaning, the actual bone at the back of the skull, and shows it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says מליקה is done 'ממול ערפו', next to the עורף and not on it. So if the משנה meant the bone itself, both שחיטה and מליקה would be invalid there. The משנה, however, said only that שחיטה is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Actual, literal
Why specifically this case?
One who pinches the neck of a bird offering
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: If you say it means the actual oref,
phrases.notes: He means the bone at the back of the skull itself.

phrases.english: why specifically one who slaughters?
Even one who pinches would also be invalid!
The Torah said 'adjacent to its oref,'
and not its oref itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא עוֹרֶף מַמָּשׁ, מַאי אִרְיָא שׁוֹחֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading עורף in the משנה as the actual bone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On the bone itself, even מליקה is invalid, so the משנה would not limit the invalid ruling to שחיטה.

steps.title: It means the area next to the bone
steps.stepSummary: עורף in the משנה means the area next to the bone, as the end of the משנה shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is 'עורף'? The area next to the עורף, as the סיפא teaches: The entire עורף is valid for מליקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's עורף means the nape, the part of the neck right below the bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the משנה says the whole עורף is valid for מליקה. Since מליקה must be done 'ממול ערפו', the משנה's עורף has to be that nearby area and not the bone itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Adjacent to, facing
The latter part of a משנה
Pinching the neck of a bird offering with the fingernail

phrases.english: Rather, what is 'oref'?
The area adjacent to the oref,
as the latter clause teaches:
The entire oref is valid for pinching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct meaning after the first one was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עורף in the משנה means the nape, the area next to the bone.
steps.whatToRemember: In this משנה, 'עורף' means the nape below the skull bone, the area 'ממול ערפו'.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that 'ממול ערפו' means the area next to the עורף.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that 'ממול' means next to the עורף. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 relied on the meaning of 'ממול ערפו'. Now the גמרא wants a source that proves this meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the meaning given in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that 'ממול' means next to the עורף, not on it.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves the meaning of 'ממול'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains 'ממול' as the place that faces the עורף and supports this with two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'ממול ערפו' means a place that faces the עורף. And so it says: 'And he dwells next to me.' And it says: 'For they turned to Me the עורף and not the face.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that defines 'ממול' and brings two פסוקים as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows that 'ממול' means near or opposite something, not the thing itself. The second פסוק is about the עורף, and the גמרא will ask next what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The place that faces it
Opposite me, near me
Face

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
'Adjacent to its oref' —
means a place that faces the oref,
And so it says:
'And he dwells adjacent to me,'
And it says:
'For they turned to Me the oref
and not the face.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.raayaObject: That 'ממול ערפו' means the area facing the עורף, not the עורף itself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with פסוקים from במדבר and ירמיהו.

steps.title: Why the second verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second פסוק adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and it says' add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed a second פסוק. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק already showed what 'ממול' means. A second proof must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is added by the extra 'and it says' proof?

phrases.english: What does 'and it says' add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the ברייתא's second פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second פסוק teaches that the first does not.

steps.title: The second פסוק locates the עורף
steps.stepSummary: The second פסוק shows where the עורף is: on the side opposite the face.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: we don't know where the עורף itself is, so how can we know where 'next to it' is? Come and hear: 'For they turned to Me the עורף and not the face.' This shows that the עורף is opposite the face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the second פסוק tells us where the עורף is, so that we know where 'next to it' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that 'ממול' means 'next to' does not help unless we know where the עורף is. The פסוק contrasts עורף with face, so the עורף is at the back of the head.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
Itself
By implication, it follows
Opposite, facing

phrases.english: And if you would say:
we don't know where the oref itself is,
so how can we know where the area next to it is —
come and hear:
'For they turned to Me the oref and not the face,'
which shows that the oref is opposite the face.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: עוֹרֶף גּוּפֵיהּ לָא יָדְעִינַן הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the second פסוק is needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק places the עורף at the back, opposite the face.
steps.whatToRemember: The first פסוק defines 'ממול' as 'next to'. The second shows that the עורף is at the back of the head.

steps.title: How מליקה is done
steps.stepSummary: The sons of רבי חייא say that in מליקה the כהן turns the סימנים toward the back of the עורף and pinches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רבי חייא say: The מצוה of מליקה: he turns the סימנים to behind the עורף and pinches.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching describes how the מצוה of מליקה is carried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סימנים, the windpipe and the food pipe, are in the front of the neck, while מליקה is done from the back. This teaching says the כהן moves the סימנים toward the back and then pinches.

keyTerms.meaning: The proper way to do a commandment
The windpipe and the food pipe
Turns, moves around

phrases.english: The sons of Rabbi Chiya say:
The מצוה of pinching:
he turns the simanim to behind the oref and pinches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: מִצְוַת מְלִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how מליקה is properly done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In מליקה, the סימנים are moved behind the עורף and then pinched.

steps.title: Two readings: allowed or required
steps.stepSummary: Some explain that turning the סימנים is allowed. Others explain that it is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: he may even turn them. And some say: he must specifically turn them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports two ways to understand the teaching of the sons of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to 'אף מחזיר', the usual way is to pinch from the back through the spine to the סימנים, and turning the סימנים is also permitted. According to 'מחזיר דוקא', turning the סימנים is the required way to do the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, also
Specifically, only this way

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that turning the סימנים is valid. They disagree only about whether it is the required way or just an allowed option.

phrases.english: Some say: he may even turn them,
and some say: he must specifically turn them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two readings of the teaching in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement over whether turning the סימנים is optional or required.

steps.title: The משנה seems to support 'even turns'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'אף מחזיר' makes more sense and begins a proof from the משנה's ruling about the עורף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it makes sense like the one who says 'he may even turn them.' From where? From what the משנה teaches: One who slaughters from the עורף, his שחיטה is invalid; one who pinches from the עורף, his מליקה is valid,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sides with the 'אף מחזיר' reading and starts to prove it from the משנה. The proof continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה calls מליקה from the עורף valid without any mention of turning the סימנים. This suggests that pinching straight from the back is the normal way and turning is only an option. The גמרא is about to spell out this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense
From where? What is the proof?
From the fact that it teaches
Invalid slaughter

phrases.english: And it makes sense like the one who says 'he may even turn them,'
From where?
From what the Mishna teaches:
One who slaughters from the oref, his slaughter is invalid;
one who pinches from the oref, his pinching is valid,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אַף מַחְזִיר, מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts deciding between the two readings in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The 'אף מחזיר' reading of the sons of רבי חייא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that מליקה from the עורף is valid.
